title: Cop shooting drives home need for tougher laws on parole: OPP
article: The vice-president of the Ontario Provincial Police Association is calling for tougher laws on parolees after a career criminal on parole was shot dead in a gun battle with police Sunday on Highway 401.
"We're always pushing for the system to be tightened up," said Sgt. Ed Kinnear. "We think the whole system is too lax."
Daniel Lamer, 37, was shot dead by OPP officers after he pulled out a gun and started shooting at them following a traffic stop Sunday morning on Highway 401, just east of Morrisburg.
Const. Dan Brisson, 28, was shot but escaped serious injury after a bullet apparently ricocheted off his bullet proof vest and grazed the back of his neck.
Two other officers on the scene were not hurt. All three officers are off on leave after the incident.
An autopsy found Lamer had been shot three times.
The province's Special Investigations Unit is investigating the shooting. It's a civilian agency which investigates any death, injury or sexual assault involving police officers.

The driver of the Pontiac Sunfire in which Lamer was a passenger, Marc Bouffard, 27, remains in custody on charges of obstructing police, giving a false name and attempting to escape custody. He returns to court on April 2.
Both Lamer and Bouffard reportedly had ties to the Hells Angels biker gang.
Lamer, who had an extensive criminal record had shot and wounded a Montreal police officer in 1991 while he was out on parole.
At the time there was a warrant for his arrest for breaching his parole conditions.
After being arrested, he was handed a 22-year jail sentence on top of the nine years left over from a 1982 conviction for kidnapping.
He was on parole when Sunday's shooting occurred.

Kinnear said police are concerned about the spread of biker gangs into Ontario, especially the Hells Angels, which has conducted a bloody war with its rivals the Rock Machine, a war which has left dozens dead in Quebec.
"These are dangerous elements and we need more powers to combat them.
"We need more powers to stop them, and to prevent them from setting up clubhouses," said Kinnear.
